igcse-0580-geometry-parallel-line-angles.description: Identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles and use the correct reasons.

sections.title: Which angles occupy the matching corner?
sections.label: Find corresponding angles
sections.intro: A transversal crosses two lines. Corresponding angles are in the same relative corner at the two crossings.

blocks.html: If the crossed lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal. Follow the same side of the transversal and the same side of each parallel line.

blocks.title: Use a marked pair of angles in parallel lines
blocks.prompt: The two horizontal lines are parallel. Find x and use the marked angles.
blocks.hint: Compare matching corners or interior angles on the same or opposite sides of the transversal.
blocks.solution:
Corresponding angles in parallel lines are equal.

The marked angle is \(52^\circ\).

blocks.html: Two angles with similar drawn sizes are not a reason for equality. Use the stated parallel lines and the angle positions.

blocks.title: Use a marked pair of angles in parallel lines
blocks.prompt: The two horizontal lines are parallel. Find x and use the marked angles.
blocks.hint: Compare matching corners or interior angles on the same or opposite sides of the transversal.
blocks.solution:
Alternate angles in parallel lines are equal.

The marked angle is \(52^\circ\).

blocks.html: Compare each crossing like two copies of the same intersection.

sections.title: Which interior angles lie on opposite sides?
sections.label: Recognise alternate angles
sections.intro: Interior angles lie between the parallel lines. An alternate pair is on opposite sides of the transversal at different crossings.

blocks.html: Alternate angles are equal when the lines are parallel. If a diagram is rotated, the side relationship still identifies the pair.

figure.alt: Two parallel lines are marked with matching arrows. A transversal crosses them and the prompt refers to the orange angles.
figure.caption: The two orange angles are between the marked parallels and on opposite sides of the transversal.

blocks.title: Use a marked pair of angles in parallel lines
blocks.prompt: The two horizontal lines are parallel. Find x and use the marked angles.
blocks.hint: Compare matching corners or interior angles on the same or opposite sides of the transversal.
blocks.solution:
Co-interior angles in parallel lines sum to 180°.

The marked angle is \(128^\circ\).

blocks.html: Looking for a remembered letter shape can obscure the relevant lines. Check the actual centre points and sides of the transversal.

blocks.title: Equate corresponding angle expressions
blocks.prompt: Two corresponding angles on parallel lines are \((2x+5)^\circ\) and \(51^\circ\). Find x.
blocks.hint: Use the relationship between the angles before solving the equation.
blocks.solution:
Corresponding angles are equal, so \(2x+5=51\).

Subtract 5 and divide by 2 to get \(x=23\).

blocks.html: Trace the transversal from one marked angle to its partner.

sections.title: When do the interior angles total 180°?
sections.label: Use co-interior angles and linked facts
sections.intro: Co-interior angles are between the parallels on the same side of the transversal. Their sizes add to \(180^\circ\).

blocks.html: When several facts are needed, find one labelled angle first. Then use equality or the straight-line sum to reach the target.

blocks.title: Know when parallel-angle rules apply
blocks.prompt: Two straight lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is \(52^\circ\). The two lines are not known to be parallel. Can you conclude its corresponding angle is the same?
blocks.hint: Check the hypothesis before applying the name of an angle rule.
blocks.solution:
Corresponding and alternate equalities used here need parallel lines.

The position of two angles alone does not establish equality.

options.A: Yes, every corresponding pair is equal
options.B: Yes, angles are always equal if they lie on two lines
options.C: No, the lines must be established as parallel

blocks.html: Co-interior angles generally differ in size. The shared result is their sum, not equality.

blocks.title: Find a supplementary angle using two linked facts
blocks.prompt: Two parallel lines meet a transversal. One angle is \(52^\circ\). Its alternate angle and x are next to each other on a straight line. Find x.
blocks.hint: Find the alternate angle first. Use the straight-line sum next.
blocks.solution:
Alternate angles are equal on parallel lines. Adjacent angles on a straight line total 180°.

The alternate angle is \(52^\circ\). The remaining angle is \(128^\circ\).

igcse-0580-geometry-polygon-angles.description: Find angle sums and side counts of regular polygons, with irregular polygons in the Extended section.

sections.title: Why do the exterior turns make one full turn?
sections.label: Walk around a regular polygon
sections.intro: As you walk round a convex polygon, turn at each corner until facing along its next side. Back at the start, the total outside turn is \(360^\circ\).

blocks.html: In a regular \(n\)-sided polygon all these exterior turns are equal. Each is \(\frac{360^\circ}{n}\). If you know the exterior angle, divide the full turn by that angle to find the side count.

blocks.title: Find a regular polygon's exterior angle
blocks.prompt: Find one exterior turning angle of a regular polygon with 6 sides.
blocks.hint: Use the full turn and the number of vertices.
blocks.solution:
One full circuit turns through 360°. The equal exterior turns share this total.

Divide \(360^\circ\) by 6. The angle is \(60^\circ\).

blocks.html: The exterior angle used here is the turn at the boundary. It is not the large reflex angle outside the polygon.

blocks.title: Find the interior angle of a regular polygon
blocks.prompt: Find one interior angle of a regular polygon with 6 sides.
blocks.hint: Find the exterior turn first or divide the total interior angle sum equally.
blocks.solution:
At each vertex, the interior angle and its exterior turn sum to 180°.

The exterior angle is \(60^\circ\). Its neighbouring interior angle is \(120^\circ\).

blocks.html: Check that your recovered side count is a whole number of at least three.

sections.title: How does an exterior turn give an interior angle?
sections.label: Use the adjacent straight line
sections.intro: At a convex vertex, the interior angle and its exterior turn make a straight angle. Find one by subtracting the other from \(180^\circ\).

blocks.html: To recover the side count from an interior angle, subtract it from \(180^\circ\) first. Use the exterior turn in the division by \(360^\circ\).

blocks.title: Recover the number of sides from an angle
blocks.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(60^\circ\). How many sides does it have?
blocks.hint: The exterior angles share the full turn, so use the exterior one to recover the side count.
blocks.solution:
The exterior turning angle is \(60^\circ\).

Divide \(360^\circ\) by \(60^\circ\) to obtain 6 sides.

sections.title: Which angle made by a diameter is a right angle?

sections.title: Which central angle is twice the angle at the circumference?
sections.label: Use the same arc
sections.intro: Take the endpoints of the arc from the two arms of the circumference angle. The relevant arc between them does not contain the angle's vertex.

blocks.title: Compare a centre angle with the circumference angle
blocks.prompt: O is the centre. The angle \(\angle ACB\) on the circle is \(34^\circ\). Find the smaller angle \(\angle AOB\) subtended by the same arc AB.
blocks.hint: Choose the central angle on the arc that does not contain C.
blocks.solution:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.

The central angle on the specified arc is twice \(34^\circ\), so it is \(68^\circ\).

An angle of 108° at the circumference subtends the same arc as a reflex central angle of 216°.

sections.title: How do I compare two chords' distances from the centre?
sections.label: Measure perpendicular distances
sections.intro: The distance from the centre to a chord is measured along a line at right angles to that chord.

blocks.title: Use equal chords to compare distances from the centre
blocks.prompt: Two chords have equal lengths. The perpendicular distance from the centre to the first chord is 3 cm. Find the perpendicular distance to the second.

blocks.html: A sloping line joining the centre to an endpoint is a radius. It is not the perpendicular distance to the chord.

blocks.solution:
Substitute the radius and perpendicular distance to get \(AM^2=13^2-12^2=25\).

sections.title: What does a shared external start tell me about tangent lengths?
sections.label: Equate two tangent lengths from one point

blocks.html: If the lengths are written as expressions, equate them and solve. A radius also meets its tangent at right angles at the contact. Use that right triangle to find one length if required.

blocks.title: Use the equality of two tangents from one point
blocks.prompt: PA and PB are tangents from an external point P. Their lengths in centimetres are \(3x+4\) and \(x+12\). Find x.
blocks.hint: The points where the tangents touch may differ, but their starting point is the same.
blocks.solution:
Tangents from the same external point have equal lengths. So \(3x+4=x+12\).

Collect x-terms and constants. This gives \(x=4\).
